title: cauchy-horizon-crossing: the tidal cost of crossing the Cauchy horizon of a regular black hole, and the passable window
description:
Reproduction package for the note Crossing the inner horizon of a regular black hole: the cost of the Cauchy horizon and the passable window. Contains the tidal-tensor integration, the shell-impulse thresholds, the convergence study in the number of shells, the Reissner–Nordström control run, and the figure of the window. Every number is reproduced by one command from a clean clone; the map from each number to its script and result file is in docs/reproducibility.md.

A body falling into a regular black hole and crossing the inner (Cauchy) horizon accumulates a finite, epoch-independent deformation — Ori's weak singularity, reproduced here for an inner-extremal profile — but receives a transverse velocity kick at the outgoing shell that grows without bound with the entry time. The crossing is therefore survivable only inside a window measured in milliseconds for stellar-mass holes and in years to millennia for supermassive ones.

Scope, stated here and not only in the repository: convergence in the number of shells is established for detuned profiles and for Reissner–Nordström, where replacing one shell by up to 1000 changes the deformation by at most 2×10-4. For the exact triple root it is not formally established: the observed variation is 2.5×10-3 to 7×10-3 and is not monotone in the number of shells, and the runs that would settle it were aborted. The triple-root evidence rests on at most 100 shells. The likely cause is bookkeeping rather than physics, and the argument for that is given in the repository.

Licensing is split: code in src/ and figures/ is MIT; data in data/, raw logs in logs/ and the generated figure images are CC-BY-4.0. See LICENSE.

The calculations were carried out with automated agents under the author's direction, with an independent cross-audit between two separate research projects. The author is responsible for the results.
